assessment.summary: A preventive file-read boundary is required before public release; the preferred restricted-root design is documented upstream but is not present in the current stable or alpha Windows App Server schemas.

nonNegotiables: Bind only to 127.0.0.1 and retain exact-origin plus pairing authorization.
Never read, parse, copy, log, or transmit Codex authentication material.
Retain no approvals, no MCP servers, no tool network, no writes, and fail-closed lifecycle behavior.
Preserve a one-time install and simple current-user activation flow without administrator rights where practical.
Do not publish while the high-severity preventive isolation finding remains unresolved unless the owner explicitly accepts the residual risk.
assumptions: The official Codex binary and OpenAI service remain trusted dependencies.
No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
The stable 0.147.0 and alpha 0.148.0-alpha.9 schemas generated on 2026-08-12 accurately represent those released App Server contracts.
A browser context at the paired Bookarium origin and all study content remain untrusted.

opportunities.title: Deny unrelated file reads before built-in tool activity
opportunities.summary: Move enforcement from post-start tool notifications to a preventive restricted-read boundary, an outer OS isolation boundary, or removal of the tutor-turn entry point.
opportunities.diagnosis: The connector owns a no-file policy but the released App Server contract gives it only broad read-only execution; the adapter learns about unsafe built-in activity after a read may already have occurred.

evidence.claim: The sealed scan validated that built-in activity is rejected only after an item event can report it.
Current source fixes an empty workspace, clears MCP configuration, uses no approvals and a read-only/no-network policy, rejects host actions, and terminates on every non-passive item.
Current official App Server documentation describes restricted read roots and externalSandbox but does not document a built-in-tool denial field.
Generated TurnStartParams schemas from stable 0.147.0 and alpha 0.148.0-alpha.9 contain neither restricted read roots nor a built-in-tool denial field.
Prompt rules and event-time termination cannot prevent file content from entering a turn if an allowed built-in read occurs before notification.

desiredInvariants: Browser-controlled study text cannot cause a process to read outside the empty connector-owned workspace.
The denial is enforced before the first read rather than after a protocol notification.
Unsupported or ignored isolation configuration fails closed without broad-read fallback.
Codex remains the sole owner and reader of its authentication state.
Reactive unsafe-item termination remains as defense in depth.

options.title: Keep the publication gate
options.summary: Retain the current runtime and block public distribution while a preventive control is unavailable.

findingCoverage.rationale: Blocking publication limits affected users but does not change the local browser-to-file attack path.

tradeoffs.assessment: Public exposure does not expand, although deliberately run local copies retain the finding.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify package, tag, release, and registry state remain unpublished and keep the release checklist gate.

tradeoffs.assessment: No runtime path changes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No benchmark is required unless current runtime controls change.

tradeoffs.assessment: No process or retained state is added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: No memory benchmark is required unless current runtime controls change.

tradeoffs.assessment: Existing local behavior is preserved.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Continue the existing unit, integration, and opt-in smoke suites.

tradeoffs.assessment: Maintainers must continuously track the blocker and prevent accidental publication.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Audit release workflow permissions and require the documented owner approval gate.

tradeoffs.assessment: No user or protocol migration occurs while the package remains unpublished.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm no published consumers require compatibility handling.

residualRisks: Developers and testers who run the connector remain exposed to the local finding.
A mistaken publication or explicit risk acceptance would expose the unchanged path.

workPackages: Keep the current release blocker explicit and verify registry/release state.
acceptanceCriteria: No public package, tag, or release is produced while the finding is unresolved.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Not applicable; this is the current interim state.

options.title: Require verified restricted roots
options.summary: Allow tutor turns only with a released Windows Codex App Server that accepts and enforces restricted readable roots.

findingCoverage.rationale: An enforced outside-root read denial prevents arbitrary user files from entering the turn even if a built-in tool starts.

tradeoffs.assessment: The documented policy is at the correct pre-read boundary, but released Windows enforcement is not yet available or validated.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Require a stable schema plus hostile outside-root canary tests across every supported Windows configuration.

tradeoffs.assessment: Policy parsing and filesystem access checks may add small turn startup or read latency without adding a process hop.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare 50 cold and 200 warm starts; review if p95 increases by more than 250 ms.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only a bounded policy and OS sandbox metadata are expected to be added.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare steady-state and peak working set; review if the candidate adds more than 25 MiB.

tradeoffs.assessment: Unsupported versions or insufficient platform roots will make explanations fail closed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise supported, unsupported, malformed, upgrade, downgrade, repair, and restart cases on clean Windows images.

tradeoffs.assessment: The project must maintain an exact compatibility gate and real Windows security canaries as Codex evolves.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Add release-candidate evidence for schema identity, candidate binary version, and canary outcomes.

tradeoffs.assessment: Older installed Codex versions must upgrade before explanations are available.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test nontechnical upgrade messaging and prove there is no broad-read fallback.

residualRisks: Built-in tools may still start and consume local resources before reactive termination.
Files intentionally or accidentally placed inside an allowed root remain readable.
Undocumented Windows platform-default roots could make the boundary broader than intended.

workPackages: Define a reviewed stable Codex compatibility contract and fail-closed prerequisite check.
Send restricted read access on every tutor turn without fallback.
Add fake-contract regressions and real Windows inside/outside-root canaries.
Update release and nontechnical support documentation.
acceptanceCriteria: A stable released Windows schema exposes the restricted-read field.
An outside-root synthetic marker cannot be read or appear in any protocol frame, answer, or log.
Unsupported or rejecting Codex versions never start a tutor turn.
Existing no-write, no-network, no-approval, no-MCP, event-limit, and confirmed-termination tests remain green.
migrationNotes: Keep publication blocked until clean-VM and packed-artifact verification passes.
Older Codex versions receive an actionable upgrade message without security fallback.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the explanation operation and restore the publication gate; never omit the restricted policy while continuing tutor turns.

options.title: Add an external OS sandbox broker
options.summary: Launch Codex through a native AppContainer or equivalent Windows boundary with explicit resource grants.

findingCoverage.rationale: A correctly configured OS process boundary would deny unrelated file access independently of built-in-tool notifications.

tradeoffs.assessment: AppContainer is a documented Windows security boundary, but the necessary Codex resource and authentication grants have not been designed or tested.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype with synthetic credentials and hostile file/process/network tests before touching a real Codex profile.

tradeoffs.assessment: A broker, IPC, capability setup, and isolated process launch can add startup latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure the same cold/warm workload as the baseline and profile broker launch plus IPC separately.

tradeoffs.assessment: A resident broker or additional process metadata increases working set.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure per-process and total peak working set during idle, startup, and active turns.

tradeoffs.assessment: Packaging, capability, IPC, Codex update, and split-lifecycle failures add new unavailable states.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject broker crash, App Server crash, update mismatch, denied runtime dependency, and interrupted uninstall.

tradeoffs.assessment: The project gains native builds, signing, architecture variants, OS compatibility, observability, and incident-response ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Produce a support matrix and rehearse install, update, rollback, and diagnostic flows on supported Windows editions.

tradeoffs.assessment: The current pure Node/npm lifecycle would require a foundational packaging and process-launch migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype the complete install-once and activation flow before accepting the architecture.

residualRisks: An overbroad capability or authentication grant can recreate the file-read exposure.
The broker becomes a new trusted native component and supply-chain target.
Windows Home, architecture, and Codex credential-store compatibility may prevent the intended user experience.

affectedComponents: Native Windows broker to be designed
workPackages: Run a disposable AppContainer/restricted-token feasibility prototype with synthetic data.
Design exact filesystem, authentication, runtime, network, and child-process capabilities.
Design signed multi-architecture packaging, IPC, lifecycle ownership, and diagnostics.
Build a Windows edition/version validation matrix before product integration.
acceptanceCriteria: The broker prevents outside-root reads, writes, unintended network, process escape, and host interaction before activity begins.
Codex authentication remains owned by the official CLI and is neither copied nor parsed by the connector.
The user flow remains supportable without administrator rights on the declared Windows matrix.
Broker and App Server process trees terminate and recover deterministically.
migrationNotes: Reject the option if the prototype requires copying credentials or silently excludes the supported consumer Windows editions.
Keep the publication gate throughout the prototype and staged rollout.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Remove the broker-enabled explanation path and return to the publication gate or disabled-explanation state.

options.title: Disable explanations
options.summary: Remove the browser-to-tutor-turn operation while retaining only safe lifecycle, pairing, and account metadata behavior if useful.

findingCoverage.rationale: No browser-controlled study text reaches a Codex turn, so the finding's entry point is removed.

tradeoffs.assessment: Removing /v1/ask eliminates the browser-prompt-to-built-in-tool dataflow.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify no HTTP route, browser flow, or internal caller can create a tutor turn.

tradeoffs.assessment: Tutor-turn startup and generation latency disappear.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Confirm remaining account and lifecycle endpoints meet current response budgets.

tradeoffs.assessment: No active turn buffers or tool processes are needed for browser use.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare idle/account-only working set with the current active-turn baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: The longest and most failure-prone browser operation is removed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run route and lifecycle suites and verify a deterministic unavailable response.

tradeoffs.assessment: Technical operation becomes simpler, but support and product messaging become harder because the connector loses its main function.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: User-test the frontend and installation copy with nontechnical learners before any public release.

tradeoffs.assessment: Frontend behavior and user expectations must change, even though the backend edit is small.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Coordinate connector and frontend releases and verify old clients receive a safe fixed response.

residualRisks: Pairing, account metadata, installation, and lifecycle surfaces remain, although they do not carry the tutor file-read path.
A later accidental re-enable without a preventive boundary would recreate the finding.

workPackages: Remove or hard-disable the explanation route and internal turn call.
Return a fixed non-sensitive compatibility response for older frontend clients if needed.
Update frontend and nontechnical documentation in the same release.
Add a release test proving browser input cannot create a tutor turn.
acceptanceCriteria: No browser-accessible operation can call CodexAppServerClient.ask.
Existing clients receive deterministic behavior without sensitive details.
Re-enabling explanations requires a separate reviewed security gate.
migrationNotes: Consider keeping the entire connector unpublished if account metadata alone has insufficient user value.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Re-enable explanations only after another preventive option has passed all acceptance criteria.

opportunities.recommendation: Keep the publication gate now, then adopt restricted roots only after a stable Windows Codex contract and hostile-read canaries prove enforcement; choose disabled explanations if release timing cannot wait.

openQuestions: Which stable Codex version first exposes restricted read access in its generated Windows App Server schema?
What exact Windows roots are added by platform defaults, and do any include user content?
Does restricted read enforcement cover every built-in subprocess and direct file API?
Can capability support be checked without starting a real tutor turn or reading authentication content?
If upstream support is delayed, does the product value justify a native AppContainer broker?
